title: You’re not cold…
paragraphs:
You’re not cold…
You’re just slowly becoming numb to God.
Because the most dangerous place to be is not rebellion…
It’s being comfortable while drifting away.

Seven churches.
Seven warnings.
One message that cuts deeper than you want to admit.
And here’s the open loop most people miss:
He was speaking to people who thought they were fine.

You can sing in church… and still lose your first love.
You can serve in ministry… and still tolerate secret sin.
You can look alive… and be spiritually dead.
Let’s talk about the part we avoid.

Not the loud sins.
Not the obvious rebellion.
The things you’ve learned to justify.
You don’t wake up one day and decide to walk away from God.

You stop praying like you used to.
You stop trembling at His Word.
Conviction feels softer.
Sin feels lighter.
Grace feels… normal.
But your heart is somewhere else.
This is exactly what Jesus exposed in the churches.
“You have abandoned the love you had at first.” (Revelation 2:4)
You’re still doing the right things…
But your heart is no longer burning.
“You have the reputation of being alive, but you are dead.” (Revelation 3:1)
“Because you are lukewarm… I will spit you out of my mouth.” (Revelation 3:16)
This is about people who think they’re okay… but aren’t.
You know where you’ve been drifting.
You know what you’ve been hiding.
You know what you’ve been tolerating.
Every warning in Revelation comes with an invitation.
“Remember therefore from where you have fallen; repent, and do the works you did at first.” (Revelation 2:5)
Some scholars interpret the seven churches as symbolic of different eras of church history.
Others see them as seven types of believers that exist in every generation.
But here’s what is not debated:
Every message ends with hope for the one who overcomes.
Now let’s get real about the Gospel.
Because this is where everything changes.
You are not saved by trying harder.
You are not restored by pretending better.
You are not made right by hiding deeper.
You are saved by Jesus Christ alone.
The same Jesus who walks among the churches…
Is the One who went to the cross for your sin.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Not when you had it together.
Turn away from the sin you’ve been managing.
Turn back to the Savior you’ve been neglecting.
Because the same Jesus who said “I will spit you out”…
“Behold, I stand at the door and knock.” (Revelation 3:20)
He’s not waiting to crush you.
Which church are you right now?

Ephesus—busy but empty?
Sardis—impressive but dead?
Laodicea—comfortable but lukewarm?
Whisper it if you have to.

From silence to surrender.
From numbness to fire.
From drifting to devotion.
